tell: An androgen receptor inhibitor whose N-desmethyl metabolite likely adds to its clinical activity, with a half-life near 3 days.

clues.text: Oral bioavailability is about 100%, and a high-fat meal makes no clinically significant difference to exposure. It is 96% protein bound and mainly metabolized by CYP2C8 and CYP3A4.
The active ingredient has a molecular weight of 477.44 and is practically insoluble in aqueous media across a wide pH range.
Approved under an NDA as 60 mg and 240 mg tablets, taken once daily.
No boxed warning and no contraindications. Fatigue and arthralgia are among the most common adverse reactions, and severe skin reactions are a warning.
Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer and non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
Binds the androgen receptor's ligand-binding domain, blocking its nuclear translocation, DNA binding and transcription.
The generic name begins with A and has eleven letters.
